researched.name: Bodal Chemicals Ltd
researched.reason: THE DAY'S BEST IDEA, AND IT WAS NEARLY MISSED - it is only in this log because the candidate list was re-derived from the finished scan file instead of the partial one triage had started from (see filings_status). Top of the scan at score 9, and the ONLY TRADE-category candidate of the day: the sole filing was an earnings-call transcript with the generic heading 'herewith submit transcript of earning call', and scan.py classified it TRADE from its body text - exactly the generic-heading path added after the OCCL miss. Reading it found something much larger than the duty. CONSOLIDATED Q2 FY27, stated by management on the call: revenue Rs 884 cr (+77% YoY), EBITDA Rs 128 cr (+197%) at a 14.4% margin, PAT Rs 81 cr (+1,259%); H1 FY27 revenue Rs 1,599 cr against Rs 959 cr (+67%), EBITDA Rs 203 cr (+114%), PAT Rs 112 cr against Rs 16 cr. BSE's own detailed results agree standalone: Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 852.66 cr and PAT Rs 80.47 cr against Rs 471.96 cr and Rs 4.20 cr a year earlier. That is far above the playbook's >=30% revenue plus PAT-growth bar. THE DRIVER IS A PRICE AND MANAGEMENT NAMES IT: 'Stricter enforcement of environmental laws has restricted the production. No significant new capacity has been added in our industry in China over the past several years... H acid has been consistently exported to China for more than a year', with dyestuff and benzene-downstream exports to China beginning 'possibly for the first time'. Bodal is the purest listed exposure: dye intermediates were Rs 562 cr of H1 revenue (Q2 Rs 345 cr, +88%), 16,956 MT produced in the half, 40% consumed captively, and the division is at 'almost optimum level' with no expansion planned. THERE IS ALSO A SECOND ENGINE THAT DOES NOT NEED THE PRICE: the Saykha benzene-downstream plant lost 'approximately INR30 crores' of EBITDA in each of the last two years, did Rs 108 cr of revenue in H1 at ~50% utilisation, is now above 85% heading to 'close to 100%', ran at 'more than INR300 crores' annualised in October and is guided to Rs 350-400 cr a year, with management expecting it 'to begin contributing to net profit from the current quarter'. VALUATION: 13.65x the BSE header trailing EPS of Rs 11.26 (a trailing year containing two near-zero quarters), 8.6x H1 FY27 consolidated PAT annualised, 6.0x the Q2 run-rate; the card prints the full two-sided table including the reversion case at ~41x. NO VOLUME EXPLOSION: vol_ratio 0.5x the 60-day median, turnover Rs 92.6 lakh/day. WHAT HOLDS IT AT MEDIUM: the price has ALREADY turned - management's own 'reached around INR1,800 levels, and then later on they corrected to around INR1,600 levels', and our Guidechem Chinese quote fell 7.3% in the week to 29-Oct-2026; visibility is one quarter ('Right now, we can see up to the month of January'); the three H-acid levels available today (management's 1,600, the Guidechem CNY 38,000/t, an X comment's 160k/tonne) disagree by roughly 3x and the transcript does not even state its unit; the stock is already +157% over a year and +122.6% over three months, 24% below its Rs 201.80 window high and -15.6% in the last month; there is Rs 800.2 cr of borrowing at 31-Mar-2026 against a Rs 1,936 cr market value; and it settles in BSE GROUP T. One more finding worth the log: the anti-dumping duty that triggered the TRADE classification has NOT worked - on TCCA, where Bodal is the sole Indian producer, 'antidumping duties on imports from China provided limited benefit as imports continued from the other countries', prices went Rs 110-120 to Rs 170 to about Rs 160, and 'if I sold in October at 160, I think my overall cost would be around 160 only'. A reader who saw only the duty headline would have had the thesis backwards.

researched.name: Jindal Drilling & Industries Ltd
researched.reason: Top of the scan at score 6 (ORDER + RESULT), and the order filing is the whole idea. ONGC issued a Notification of Award on 6-Nov-2026 for the company-OWNED rig Discovery-I, three years at an Effective Day Rate of Rs 51,99,293.21 / USD 54,633.36. Read from the letter itself (both the BSE and NSE copies): Rs 51,99,293.21 x 1,095 days = Rs 569.3 cr of contract value, which is 57% of FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 996.57 cr - the bucket the 2026-09-22 order study found reached 2x within two years 35.7% of the time against 21.4% for orders under 10% of sales. Against market cap it is 38%, stated only because the same study found order/market-cap predicts nothing. RARITY: reading every BSE filing for the scrip from 6-Nov-2024 to 5-Nov-2026 (126 filings, no window refused) gives TWO prior order announcements in two years - 7-May-2025 (Jindal Explorer, USD 35,138.71) and 30-Jul-2026 (Jindal Pioneer, USD 47,893.99) - so this is a once-a-year filer near the rare end of the scale, not an EPC serial bidder. NO volume explosion: vol_ratio 1.0, turnover Rs 60 lakh/day, and the stock closed -0.5% on the day and is -17.1% over the 65-day window, so the alarm bell the study warns about is absent. WHAT MAKES IT AN IDEA RATHER THAN A HEADLINE: the Q1 FY27 presentation of 10-Aug-2026 publishes the fleet rig by rig with day rates, and Discovery-I's old contract was May-23 -> Oct-26 at USD 48,324, so this is a RE-CONTRACT AT A 13.1% HIGHER RATE of a rig that was about to go idle - and on the same call the CFO had said the previous re-contract disappointed: 'We had participated with a rate of $62,000, and we were pushed down to $47,800 approximately.' Successive awards read from the company's own letters run USD 35,139 (2025) -> 47,894 (Jul-2026) -> 54,633 (today). WHAT KEEPS IT AT MEDIUM, NOT HIGH: the arithmetic in the card shows the four rigs that now have contracts add to about Rs 788 cr of FY28 rig revenue at 365 days, roughly 21% BELOW FY26's Rs 996.57 cr, because Virtue-I (USD 80,633) and Jindal Star (USD 44,000) were de-hired and no new contract has been filed for either. This award repairs a hole; it does not by itself create growth. Add 4-6 months of refurbishment with no revenue and Rs 90-110 cr of refurbishment cost per rig (CFO, same call), a single customer that sets the price through per-rig tenders, and a Rs 163 cr contingent repayment to that customer if ONGC wins in the Supreme Court (original receivable Rs 63 cr, money already received) which has already whipsawed reported profit once (+Rs 120.7 cr in Q2 FY26, -Rs 48.9 cr in Q3 FY26). Trades at a BSE header PE of 8.86 with net cash of about Rs 179 cr (gross debt Rs 52 cr + WC Rs 17 cr against liquid investments Rs 248 cr, Q1 FY27 deck slide 11) and promoter holding up from 64.40% to 66.78% over the year.

Measured consequences before it was fixed: scan.py printed 'scan SELFTEST FAIL - OCCL 30-Sep-2026 anti-dumping duty raise, generic subject: got []' TWICE (it cannot classify a generic heading without PDF text - the exact miss the selftest exists to prevent), and minsteel.py died with ModuleNotFoundError. FIXED IN THIS RUN by `python3 -m pip install "pymupdf<2"` (1.28.2) plus `find scripts/ideas/_cache -name '*.txt' -size 0 -delete`, after which the selftest PASSED. The prompt's step-0 line needs to become `python3 -m pip install "pymupdf<2"`.
